faqs.question: What does the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – BAL / Other Respiratory Sample measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) in respiratory samples using a fluorescent stain.

faqs.question: Why is the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – BAL / Other Respiratory Sample done?
faqs.answer: This test is mainly done to diagnose TB infection. It helps healthcare providers identify the presence of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) in respiratory samples, aiding in accurate diagnosis and appropriate treatment.

faqs.question: When is the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – BAL / Other Respiratory Sample recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test may be recommended if you have symptoms such as persistent cough, fever, weight loss, or night sweats, which could indicate TB infection. It is also recommended if you have been exposed to someone with TB or if you are at a higher risk of developing TB due to certain medical conditions or immunocompromised status.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – BAL / Other Respiratory Sample are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results of this test indicate the presence of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) in your respiratory sample, suggesting a possible TB infection.

faqs.question: What to expect during the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – BAL / Other Respiratory Sample?
faqs.answer: During this test, a small amount of your respiratory sample is collected using a sterile, leak-proof container. The sample is sent to the laboratory for processing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – BAL / Other Respiratory Sample?
faqs.answer: • Inform your healthcare provider about any medications you are taking. • Follow any specific instructions regarding fasting or avoiding certain foods or drinks before the test. • Provide a complete clinical history and relevant information as requested by your healthcare provider. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – BAL / Other Respiratory Sample?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – BAL / Other Respiratory Sample include: • TB culture: This test helps in identifying the specific strain of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and its antibiotic sensitivity. • Chest X-ray: This imaging test provides additional information about lung involvement in TB infection.

faqs.question: What is the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – BAL / Other Respiratory Sample also known as?
faqs.answer: Fluorescent Stain for Acid-Fast Bacilli examination, TB smear test

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis (TB)?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by the bacteria Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body, such as the kidneys, spine, or brain.
